A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research lineage, despite substantial changes to the method, benchmark and title. All 20 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v2, including figures, equations, tables and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original QA experiments, component ablations, neuron-activation analyses and human validation of CoConflictQA.

after.justification: V2 reports original QA experiments, activation interventions, sensitivity analyses and human validation of CoFaithfulQA.

M1.justification: V1 prunes FFNs selected by activation decreases after adding context. V2 instead selects layers using activation differences between faithful and unfaithful responses, then scales the selected FFNs' activations, defaulting to eight fully suppressed layers. The knowledge-augmented training and preference-optimization losses remain.

E1.justification: The six underlying QA datasets and three ConFiQA tasks remain. CoFaithfulQA additionally retains a faithful, nonconflicting population for activation and intervention analyses, whereas CoConflictQA discards nonconflicting instances. Main benchmark evaluation still targets conflicting cases.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 add COIECD and DDR to the retained comparator set; DPO becomes C-DPO. The parameter-level comparator also changes substantively: v1 describes pruning low-importance weights, while v2 Appendix A.10 describes suppressing the highest-saliency weights.

E3.justification: Conflict verification changes from GPT-4o-mini to agreement between GPT-4o and GLM-4-plus, with revised retained samples. Human validation increases from 600 to 900 examples. EM is dropped, and new intervention and hyperparameter experiments introduce controlled suppression settings. The reported training sample count, steps, batch size and learning rate remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds faithful-versus-unfaithful activation comparisons, causal interventions, bottom/middle/random layer-selection controls, and sensitivity tests for suppression strength, layer count and loss weights. It also examines activation strength versus memory reliance. V1's context-versus-no-context activation profiles across model families are removed; knowledge-use and consistency-filtering analyses remain.

E5.justification: V2 adds Pearson-correlation significance reporting at p < 0.05, Cohen's kappa of 0.766 using a multiply annotated subset, and error bars in Figure 1(c), whose meaning is unspecified. Neither version reports repeated-training-run uncertainty for benchmark scores.

E6.justification: Benchmark and ablation scores change extensively. Reported average ConR is 71.50 for PIP-KAG on CoConflictQA versus 69.54 for ParamMute on CoFaithfulQA; changed methods and data prevent interpreting this as a same-setting performance loss. Human–judge agreement changes from 85.6% to 90.4% under revised validation. New intervention results appear, while EM and parameter-count results disappear.

T1.justification: The activation-gap definition changes from a query/context difference to an expected response-activation difference between faithful and unfaithful subsets. V2 formalizes top-N selection and activation scaling. The underlying FFN equations and adaptation objectives are retained; neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from uninstalling knowledge through parameter pruning to identifying unfaithfulness-associated FFNs and controlling their activation. V2 foregrounds a mechanistic account of unfaithful RAG generation and removes the abstract's quantified 13% parameter-reduction claim, although generic efficiency language survives in the appendix.

C2.justification: V1 interprets its findings as removing stored knowledge; v2 advances causal explanations involving overactive FFNs. V2 adds limitations concerning excessive suppression, retrieval failures and model scale, while dropping v1's rule-based-metric caveat. Appendix A.3 gives contradictory interpretations of suppression's effect on faithful-subset NLL.

D1.justification: V2 adds suppression implementation, DDR preference-construction and annotator-training details. It omits v1's LoRA rank/scaling values and per-model selected-layer listing. The abstract replaces an explicit available-code repository link with a future GitHub release statement; most training budgets and prompt templates remain documented.

R1.justification: Positioning shifts from pruning and parameter-efficient KAG toward mechanistic explanations of RAG unfaithfulness. V2 adds substantive discussion of Jin et al.'s attention-head interventions and Sun et al.'s ReDEEP, alongside other new citations. The Asai/Borgeaud framing around smaller retrieval-equipped models is removed.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and much explanatory prose are rewritten, with systematic method and benchmark renaming. A preliminary mechanistic study now precedes the method, related work moves from Section 2 to Section 7, and ethics and limitations are reorganized into the appendices.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column formatting. V1's method illustrations and model-family activation plots disappear; v2 adds intervention and sensitivity figures, expands the ablation table, and removes EM/parameter columns. Existing knowledge-use panels are rearranged, and the model-family performance figures are merged.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful interventions, layer-selection controls and stronger annotation checks. However, its Figure 7 retains LLaMA3-8B ConR of 71.5 while Table 7 reports 69.54; these displays agreed in v1. V2 also gives conflicting NQ counts of 572 and 1,409 and opposing faithful-subset NLL interpretations in Appendix A.3. These inconsistencies affect the benchmark and central mechanism evidence, preventing a reliable judgment of net quality improvement.
